name: Zenaida Arizpe
languages: Enough German to scold the freighters from Castroville
equipment: Buckskin coat, short, over a man's linen shirt with the sleeves rolled
Repeating rifle (Winchester '66), 12 rounds loaded, kept in the ferry shelter on whichever bank she is on
Navy revolver, 6 rounds loaded, in a sash
Hatchet, for the ferry rope, kindling, and anyone who tries to cut the rope before she does
The ferry: a flatboat on a hemp rope, a dugout canoe, two long poles, and her nephew Ignacio, 15
Her Texas ferry license (contested by Sheriff Purcell) and her Mexican ferry license (contested by Capitán Galván), in an oilcloth packet
A ledger of everyone she has carried across in two years, in her own shorthand, which nobody else can read
Saddle and tack, canteen (2), a straw sombrero
Riding horse: a sturdy bay mare called Ventisca who swims better than most men
features: Both Sides of the River (Borderlands origin: English and Spanish natively; she knows every ford, every boatman and every customs inspector for fifty miles of the river on both banks; advantage on Persuasion and Insight with border people of either side)

Trailcraft (Scout: never lost on terrain she has crossed before; she finds water each day without a check wherever there is any; she can follow a trail at a normal pace and read the sign; on the river she knows where the bottom is firm and where it is not)
Long Shot (Scout: no disadvantage at long range with a Longarm if she Aimed first that turn; proficiency doubled for Perception to spot something more than 300 ft away, across the river for instance)

Ghost on the Range (Scout, 2nd level: in natural terrain, including the cane brakes of the riverbank, she can Hide as a bonus action even when only lightly obscured, and leaves no trail anyone without Trailcraft can follow)
Path: Army Scout (Scout, 3rd level: she scouted for Sheriff Uresti's deputies after stock thieves; once per day of travel she rides ahead and the GM tells her the next trail event before it happens)
Ability Score Improvement (Scout, 4th level: +1 Dexterity, +1 Wisdom)

The Mail Road (Stage Driver background: she drove the Laredo-Crow's Ford mail for six years before she bought the ferry; every station keeper and hostler on the river road knows her, will change her horses and tell her who rode through, and she can drive any team without a check)

personality.traits: I charge everyone the same and Texans with guns more. I know everyone's business and tell nobody's. I laugh loudly and often and at the wrong people. I am not afraid of the river and I am a little afraid of my nephew's mother.
personality.ideals: A river is a road, not a wall. People have crossed here to visit their cousins since before there was a Texas or a Mexico, and they will after. I carry them.
personality.bonds: My ferry, my nephew Ignacio, whom I am raising since my sister died, and my two licenses, one from each government, each of which the other government says is worthless. Sheriff Uresti, who never once asked me who I had carried. Isom and Inés Haywood, whose children I carried across for their baptism.
personality.flaws: Both sheriffs and the captain have threatened my licenses, and the boat is everything I own. I have told myself I will not be anyone's informant. I have not been tested yet.

appearance: A tall, broad-shouldered, sun-browned woman of thirty-nine with a wide face, laugh lines, strong hands blistered by the ferry rope, and grey-shot black hair tied up under a straw sombrero. A short buckskin coat, a red sash with a revolver in it, rolled sleeves, bare feet on the boat and boots on land.
backstory: Zenaida Arizpe was born in Villa del Cuervo in 1835, the daughter of a freighter, and grew up on the road between Laredo and Matamoros on her father's wagons. She married a stage driver, drove the Laredo-Crow's Ford mail with him and then, after he was killed in a wreck at the Arroyo Salado in 1866, alone, for six years, which nobody had seen a woman do and everybody got used to. In 1872 she bought the Crow's Ford ferry with her savings and has run it ever since, a flatboat on a rope between two countries, with her nephew Ignacio. She holds a license from the county under Sheriff Uresti and one from the municipality of Villa del Cuervo; Sheriff Purcell says the first is void and Capitán Galván says she needs his permission for the second. She carried Isom and Inés Haywood and their children across for the children's baptisms at San Isidro, and has carried Inés back and forth a dozen times since April. She knows exactly where Palomas Bend is, and she knows the ford there.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Zenaida is the party's key to the river in lb-scenario-003 and lb-scenario-004. Introduce her at the ferry on Thursday: loud, funny, expensive and immovable. She will not tell anyone with a poster about Palomas Bend (CLUE D6c) until they have earned it by freeing Dámaso, standing up to Purcell, or carrying Doña Refugio's or Uresti's word. Then she is a companion: she can carry anyone across at any hour, knows every ford for twenty miles, can speak for the party to Don Evaristo and Capitán Galván, and can take them to Palomas Bend by the Mexican bank where the Riders cannot follow. In lb-scenario-004 she brings the dugout to the Palomas ford for the children, or the ferry down to Rio Grande City by river if the road is closed. She will not fight on the Mexican bank against Mexican soldiers, ever.
dmNotes.voice: Loud, warm, quick, mixing Spanish and English in the same sentence without noticing; calls everyone 'hijo' or 'hija' regardless of age; swears colorfully in both languages and a little German.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: her ferry and her two licenses, honored by both banks. Secondary: Ignacio's future, which she would like to be a schoolteacher's and not a boatman's. Tertiary: Isom, Inés and their children, whom she loves and will not say so.
dmNotes.secrets: Her ledger records everyone she has carried in two years, in a shorthand only she can read, including a night in mid-February when a pale man on a grey horse crossed to Villa del Cuervo and back asking which of the Cantú families had a daughter married to a Black soldier. Vandiver sent Gattis to the border that month, as soon as the judge began building his case, to learn where Isom would run. Shown Gattis, she will remember him, and the date in her ledger is evidence that the Vandivers were hunting Isom's family seven weeks before the murder.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: commercial, then curious, then fond. Toward Uresti: trust. Toward Purcell: amused contempt. Toward Capitán Galván: respect and exasperation. Toward Don Evaristo: an old ally. Toward the Riders: she will cut the rope in the middle of the river before she carries one of them across.
